title: An Israeli AI startup says it cracked a 38 year old graph theory bound for $2,000
key_facts: Israeli startup doubleAI says its autonomous Double Agent system improved a graph theory girth bound that stood since 1988.
The best earlier explicit constructions (Margulis; Lubotzky, Phillips and Sarnak) reached a girth coefficient of 4/3; Double Agent reached 8/5, the theoretical ceiling being 2.
It reportedly used under $2,000 of computing with no human steering the maths.
The proof is written in the Lean proof assistant, so others can check it.
Girth matters for building low-density parity-check error-correcting codes.
Nothing has been peer reviewed; the 'first improvement in 38 years' framing should be treated as the company's claim.
doubleAI is led by Mobileye co-founder Amnon Shashua of Hebrew University.
quote_evidence: Nothing about this result has gone through peer review yet, and extremal graph theory is a field with a small number of experts who will need time to pick the construction apart, Lean formalization or not.
Treat the "first improvement in 38 years" framing as doubleAI's claim until independent mathematicians weigh in publicly.
why_it_matters_hint: If it holds, a cheap AI run moved a decades-old maths bound that feeds error-correcting codes.
notes: Full text read. Startup Fortune relays a Calcalist report (Calcalist not read directly). Company claim, not peer reviewed.
